overall_safety_summary: The user is bending down to retrieve a pan from a low cabinet while wearing open-toed sandals, which presents mild risks of physical strain, balance loss, and foot injury from dropped objects.

hazards.description: Retrieving cookware from a very low cabinet shelf near floor level.
hazards.explanation: Bending down deeply to lift objects can cause back strain or a loss of balance.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults are more susceptible to balance loss, dizziness upon bending, and musculoskeletal strain.
hazards.recommended_action: Store heavy or frequently used cookware on waist-level shelves or in pull-out drawers to minimize deep bending.

hazards.description: Wearing open-toed sandals while handling heavy cookware in the kitchen.
hazards.explanation: Open-toed footwear provides no protection if a heavy pan is accidentally dropped.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults have more fragile skin and a higher risk of severe injury or complications from impact wounds on the feet.
hazards.recommended_action: Wear closed-toe, supportive shoes with non-slip soles when working in the kitchen.

uncertainties: The weight and exact material of the pan being retrieved are not fully clear from the visual angle.
